title: Later Liang Dynasty
capsule: The Later Liang (907–923) was the first of the Five Dynasties, founded when the warlord Zhu Wen (Zhu Quanzhong) deposed Emperor Ai of Tang in 907, extinguishing the Tang dynasty and ruling from Kaifeng over the Yellow River heartland. Zhu Wen was murdered by his own son in 912, and the dynasty spent its short life locked in war with the rival Shatuo Turk regime of Jin under Li Keyong and his son Li Cunxu. In 923 Li Cunxu proclaimed the Later Tang and took Kaifeng; the last Liang emperor, Zhu Youzhen, took his own life as the city fell.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Liang is documented in the official Chinese dynastic histories (Liangshu), providing clear administrative records for the core Yangtze territories; frontier zones, particularly in the Sichuan basin and vis-a-vis the Northern Wei and Western Wei, are less precisely mapped.
